dead-letter:email-q.title: email has no dead-letter queue
dead-letter:email-q.message: If Email sender can't handle a message, it's dropped after 3 deliveries. A command queue is where losing messages hurts most.
dead-letter:email-q.rationale: A message that keeps failing is redelivered up to the broker's delivery limit, then goes to the broker's dead-letter route, or is dropped when there isn't one (or its filter doesn't take the message). A dead-letter queue keeps it to inspect and replay.

secret-identity:key-vault.title: 2 services read secrets without an identity
secret-identity:key-vault.message: Email sender and SMS rate limiter read secrets from notify-kv, but the diagram doesn't say what they sign in as. With a managed identity, they get in with no stored credential to leak or rotate.
secret-identity:key-vault.rationale: A service needs a credential to open a vault, and one stored with the service is just one more secret. A workload identity (an Azure managed identity, an AWS IAM role, a Google Cloud service account) signs it in with nothing to store or rotate, and one per service gives each only the access it needs (least privilege).
